h: The Gates of Teshuvah Are Always Open

p: "and He said to me: Enough for you;
At the beginning of the parsha it says
what does one matter have to do with the other?
according to their statement, of blessed memory
that is, in its literal sense:
that from now on he will be good
And it says in the Midrash Rabbah
'the trust of all the ends of the earth
so too the gates of prayer, etc.;
כָּךְ יָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
so the hand of the Holy One, blessed is He,
only at a time of favor,
but when the water dries up
and it falls somewhat short of the measure of a mikveh,
גַּם אִם יְצַמְצֵם אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּגוּפוֹ
even if he compresses his body
the immersion does not count for him.
is the waters of the source,
And this is as written by
that would be removed by water, etc.;
there is an allusion in the matter:
so one who directs his heart
from the impurities of souls, etc.,
That is, when he does teshuvah
from the depth of the inwardness of his heart,
he reaches the root and the source,
"For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem
as the waters cover the sea";
and willful sins become like merits.
וְהוּא בְּחִינַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is the aspect of David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
"The word of the man raised on high"
"who raised up the yoke of teshuvah"
for he became like a new creation,
"Create in me a pure heart, O God";
and that is the matter of creation something from nothing.
And on the root of this allusion
which held one hundred and fifty
that this matter is alluded to
about a certain student that Rabbi Meir had
who would declare the sheretz pure
with one hundred and fifty reasons;
in declaring pure, with empty argumentation,
However, according to what is known from Chazal,
to the impurity of a sheretz,
"immersing with a sheretz in his hand";
and also the statement of Chazal
and all were given to Moshe
allude to the seven holy attributes;
and they were all handed to Moshe
and it is the aspect of teshuvah
from the depth of the heart,
which is from the supernal source
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who is the aspect of a complete tzaddik;
and in the place where baalei teshuvah stand,

p: It is known from the Arizal
that there are three impure kelipos
and they are alluded to in the pasuk (Yechezkel 1:4):
of all kinds of impure animals
of all kinds of permitted desires,
And from the root of the three kelipos mentioned above
an aspect of admixture of evil;
they are the Ofanim, Chayos and Serafim;
and in the soul of man
they are nefesh, ruach and neshamah,
which can be blemished by prohibitions
עַל יְדֵי שׁוֹרֶשׁ ג׳ קְלִיפּוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
through the root of the three kelipos mentioned above;
Now if a person has blemished
and corrupted even in his three aspects,
namely in his mind, his heart
which are of the aspect of nefesh, ruach and neshamah,
in all the seven holy attributes
that is, forty-nine gates in each one
from the depth of the heart,
And this is what Chazal alluded to
who could declare the sheretz pure:
to the three impure kelipos in general;
גַּם אִם נִטְמָא הָאָדָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
even if a person has become impure, chas v'shalom,
it is nevertheless in his power
And this is the meaning of
that is, with three fiftieth gates,
Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, made
one hundred and fifty purifying mikva'os;
for then the moon stood in its fullness,
only sin caused it to be otherwise,
until the time of the End.
Let us return to our matter:
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
in the forty-nine gates of understanding,
which are according to the way of the Torah;
therefore his prayer did not succeed
Enough for you; do not continue," etc.
which is alluded to in the expression "and now,"
one can accomplish the rectification of everything;
